round1_ask_classification.ask: Positive resume leg: panel at A, kill after first AdvanceBranchExpectedOld (marker==tip==C), re-run without foreign commit converges without tripping stale-SHA (G5, second half).
round1_ask_classification.classification: DISCHARGED — delivered as leg xxii; the disclosed adaptation (S-stage advance killed instead of the M-stage one the consolidation literally named) is JUDGED VALID.
round1_ask_classification.judgment: I read internal/panel/gate.go's Req-11 dirty-tree clause (7) directly: whenever a panel is registered and f.UserDirt is non-empty, the gate BLOCKS (artifact dirt is filtered out by the caller before the clause, so only USER dirt trips it). The claimed mutual exclusivity is real and two-step: (1) under a live panel, run 1 cannot carry uncommitted user dirt past the panel gate; (2) with no user dirt, the M-stage snapshot (which excludes materializedArtifactPaths) equals the tip tree, so changedFromTip is empty and M ELIDES — an M-stage advance is therefore structurally unreachable under a live registered panel, in production as in the fixture. The artifact-sync stage is the only stage a panel-registered kill-resume can exercise, and it is the production-faithful shape (artifact dirt is exempt from clause 7 per ADR-0025). The property is identically asserted: Run's step-2.25 panel-gate skip is guarded by resumeStage == "" alone — verified stage-agnostic in ad08acf7's complete.go (the guard is untouched by the fix commit; only CAS-clear plumbing changed there) — so which stage's advance gets killed does not change what the leg proves. Leg xxii itself asserts every element of my ask: a REAL panel registered at A with 6 APPROVE verdicts and ReviewedHeadSHA=A; the kill leaves marker==tip==D verified by explicit readMarker assertions (oid==dCommit, stage==artifact-sync) with dCommit != A asserted; the plain re-run converges (BeadClosed, bead branch a real ancestor of the spec branch, marker cleared) — a stale-SHA regression at step 2.25 would fail this leg with the gate's own block message. Passed live in my run. Note the fixture even routes checkDirtyTreeFn through the REAL next.CheckDirtyTreeDetail, so the artifact-only classification is measured, not stubbed.

mock_realism_fixes: All three verified honest. (1) TestRun_AutoCommitMaterializesViaSnapshot now distinguishes the M-stage snapshot (exclude non-empty) from the S-stage one (no exclusions) and returns an EMPTY S-delta — this models production exactly (G1's changedFromCurrent is measured against the post-advance tip, which already contains M's content), and the original assertions (MaterializeStageCommit targeting the matched bead worktree, stage=materialization, AdvanceBranchExpectedOld on bead/bead-1) are unchanged. (2) TestRun_CommitMsgWithArtifactDirtBuildsBothStages narrows the S-delta to the artifact path alone for the same reason — the old both-paths shape would now (correctly) trip G1's non-artifact-delta refusal, so the change reflects the new contract rather than dodging it; G1's mechanics are pinned by real git in leg xxi regardless. (3) TestPerBeadGatesAnchorToBeadFork_MainDriftDoesNotBlock drops the base==fork-sha discriminant from the mock's ROUTING — my initial worry was that a wrong-base gate call would now return clean and slip through, but the test's tail retains the fork-anchoring pin POSITIVELY: it filters recorded ChangedFilesTree calls to base==fork-sha, asserts exact workdir/treeOID on each, and FAILS if fewer than two such calls occurred (one per gate lane) — a gate that regressed to a wrong base yields gateCalls < 2 and the test fails. The pin moved from return-value routing to call-shape assertion; nothing was lost.
rationale: My round-1 ask is discharged and the adaptation argument survives direct verification against the Req-11 clause; the three mock-realism fixes are honest; all suites I ran are green at ad08acf7 (all 24 leg tests including xxi/xxii/xxiii; internal/complete -short; executor; gitutil; lint ratchets; guard; the ADR-0041 pinning tests) and the worktree was left clean at the reviewed commit. The G1-G4 code I read is well-formed (closed stage set with duplicate-trailer-reads-as-absent, propagated discriminator errors, CAS clear against the observed OID, delta-refusal at the exact tree about to be committed). Why REQUEST_CHANGES rather than APPROVE: one NEW ratchet-honesty drift introduced by this very fix commit, plus my two round-1 riders which the consolidation dropped without being fixed, refuted, or filed — and one of them got objectively worse in this commit. All three are prose-only, sub-ten-minute fixes; none is a hard block.
